title: Fahrenheit 451, Bradbury
subject: litterature
description: In this future, firefighters burn books. Guy Montag discovers that culture disappears through indifference as much as through censorship.

hero.hook: 451°F: the temperature where paper catches fire, and a society gives up thinking.

blocks.text: Published in **1953**, **Fahrenheit 451** is a pillar of the **dystopia**. This genre describes a future society where the individual is oppressed. **Ray Bradbury**, born in **1920** and died in **2012**, imagines a future where firefighters burn books deemed dangerous for social stability. The title refers to the temperature at which the paper ignites, approximately 233°C.

More than a criticism of state censorship, the work shows a population which voluntarily abandons reading in favor of empty entertainment and technological immediacy. Bradbury warns: freedom of thought is lost as much by forgetting as by force.

sections.title: Genesis of a visionary work under tension

blocks.text: The novel was born in the context of , between **1950** and **1954**. It is a time of anti-communist witch hunt in the United States. Artists and writers were blacklisted. Bradbury nuance, however: the threat also comes from television and . Products become standardized and the desire to purchase is constantly stimulated. blocks.caption: Ray Bradbury, author who wrote his novel about censorship in a library.

blocks.text: Bradbury wrote Fahrenheit 451 in 9 days on a typewriter rented from a university library, at 10 cents for 30 minutes.

Unlike , Orwell's novel where oppression comes from a dictator monitoring every move, here it is the citizens themselves who have given up on books. They do it out of comfort and fear of debate. Censorship has become a collective choice, not just an imposition. [[1984]]

sections.title: The Montag system: the fire of knowledge

blocks.text: **Guy Montag** is a firefighter: his job is to burn underground libraries. His wife **Mildred** spends her days in front of the **parlors**, wall-mounted screens that cover entire walls. It is absorbed by empty emissions. His neighbor **Clarisse** reminds him that firefighters used to put out fires.

blocks.caption: Burning the books: the historical image that Bradbury transforms into a future dystopia.

blocks.text: Montag steals books. His opponent, Captain **Beatty**, knows the classics but burns them with fervor. For him, books create anxiety by revealing inequalities and contradictions. Clarisse disappears, probably killed by an automated vehicle. The world no longer has room for people who ask questions.

Tracked by the **Mechanical Bloodhound**, a police robot, Montag joins a community of intellectuals in exile. Everyone memorizes an entire book to transmit it orally: Plato's *Republic*, Shakespeare, the Bible. Culture survives in heads, not on paper.
We are books. We were hit by fire, but we survived.

Montag becomes the custodian of the **Ecclesiastes**. The novel ends with a nuclear war which destroys the city, but the resistance fighters return to the ruins. Culture can rise from its ashes if humanity agrees to think again.

Bradbury anticipated flat screens, wireless headphones and the . Some people are so saturated with fast media that they no longer want to read. In the novel, the texts are shortened until they disappear in favor of rapid images. [[entertainment society and fragmented attention]]
Bradbury describes radio “seashells” in the ear, isolating the individual from their environment, fifty years before modern wireless headphones.

Irony: this indictment against censorship has itself been amputated in certain school editions. The fight for the integrity of the work remains ongoing. **Fahrenheit 451** reminds us that freedom of thought is lost not only by force, but also by forgetfulness and intellectual laziness.
**Fahrenheit 451** shows that freedom of thought is lost not only by force, but also by forgetfulness, entertainment and intellectual laziness.
